models_evaluated: multimodal transformer (clinical data + MRI) for lymph node metastasis prediction in rectal cancer

links.outcome: Whether attention-map agreement with physician understanding improved uncertainty estimation and model reliability
links.effect: Human-in-the-loop uncertainty (variance plus attention-map agreement with physicians) showed no significant advantage over standalone variance-based uncertainty; the anticipated benefit of explanation was not confirmed.
links.quote: Our findings revealed no significant advantage of the human-in-the-loop approach over the standalone one.

links.outcome: Whether superficial attention-map explanations mislead physicians into trusting uncertain predictions
links.effect: Authors conclude superficial explanations could do more harm than good by misleading physicians into relying on uncertain predictions; attention mechanisms should not be overestimated for explainability.
links.quote: Superficial explanations could do more harm than good by misleading physicians into relying on uncertain predictions, suggesting that the current state of attention mechanisms should not be overestimated in the context of model explainability.
